angle: Texas large-load rules: power and miners
summary: Texas large-load regime as of 27 Nov 2026 is a stack of gubernatorial directives, PUCT rules and an ERCOT study rather than one statute. The next binding test is ERCOT's Batch Zero verification report due 10 Dec, taken up at the PUCT open meeting on 17 Dec. Abbott's directives still control the energization pause, while TCEQ resumed air and water permit review on 16-17 Nov. Hinojosa takes office 19 Jan and has pledged her own moratorium, whose reach is undefined. The most underexamined angle is non-AI collateral: crypto miners at or above 75 MW, other permit filers on the TCEQ e-filing system, and Texas power producers whose forward prices assume data-centre load. Queue figures and Batch Zero counts conflict across sources and are unreconciled.

angle: NVIDIA Nov 17 print and CEO-exit fallout
summary: Premise correction: Huang resigned as CEO on Nov 12 and Kress was interim CEO for about 11 days. The board reinstated Huang on Nov 22-24 (date needs confirmation) and Kress remains CFO. The Nov 17 print was Kress's first report as CEO. Q3 revenue was $115.8B and the Q4 guide was $130B, excluding China data-center compute. Probes reach Nvidia itself via the SEC, the California AG and the board special committee. The DOJ link to Nvidia is unverified. Post-print export rules and a reported halt on server shipments to Southeast Asia (SEA) are the biggest open question for the Q4 number. The 10-Q is due Dec 4. Equity has priced much of the governance discount, while ODMs, memory and optical names are less clearly priced.

angle: Oil/Hormuz post-midterm peace track
summary: Brent dipped below $94 on 26 Nov then settled at $96.57 (+2.07%), with the bounce driven by Gulf attacks rather than diplomacy. Iran still says no talks until seven conditions are met, and Hormuz traffic remains roughly half to two-thirds below pre-war levels. Only mediators relaying messages (Pakistan, Qatar) show any process. Mine-clearing claims are contested: IRGC claims are not independently confirmed, while CENTCOM says transit routes are clear. Transit counts are complicated by unverifiable US-facilitated transits. Winners and losers from a deal are identifiable: US Gulf refiners and tanker owners lose freight-driven edge, while airlines gain from lower jet fuel. OPEC+ meets 29 Nov and the January Brent contract expires 30 Nov.

Freight, not crude, is the main margin driver for US Gulf refiners, so a peace deal would hit that edge more than crude prices.
IRGC mine-sinking claims appear to be a pressure instrument rather than a verifiable count: attacks are verified, sinkings are not.
Bilateral safe-passage deals may be creating a two-tier Gulf market, which Kpler calls an informal toll, so a deal may not be needed to move barrels.

angle: Midterm results: policy winners and losers
summary: Democrats won both the House and the Senate in the Nov 3 midterms, but the power shift does not take effect until Jan 3, 2027. The lame-duck Congress is still Republican-led, with a Dec. 11 funding deadline in between, so most 'Democrats will block X' stories are 2027 events and several near-term moves are being made by the outgoing majority. Data centres and power names repriced most sharply and fastest, with contractors and miners hit harder than power producers. Defense fell on a shrinking budget, though a pending war supplemental could keep it alive. Crypto was already weak after the CLARITY Act failed cloture in September. Prediction markets face a Senate-passed death-contract ban and state litigation. Healthcare shows minimal repricing. Price data is approximate and inconsistent across sources (e.g., CEG ~$235 vs $280) and must be re-pulled before trading.

angle: PD-(L)1xVEGF class after the ivonescimab CRL

The FDA did not reject PFS-only designs as a category; it asked for a new multiregional, well-controlled trial. The read-through is mainly to the class's regulatory bar on OS and regional applicability. The nearest swing factor for SMMT is HARMONi-3 squamous, due by year-end 2026. SMMT's cash runway is no longer the binding constraint after the AstraZeneca $2B preferred investment closed on 5 Oct; the overhang is the roughly 109M-share preferred conversion and the ATM. It follows 1-for-200 (Mar 24, 2026), 1-for-20 (Jul 17, 2026) and 1-for-15 (Oct 5, 2026) splits, a cumulative ratio of about 900,000:1 by Dec 1. Recent conversions priced below $0.37, and the Series B terms for the Direct Midstream deal could not be retrieved, so dilution cannot be fully modeled.

angle: Summit ivonescimab CRL: Nov 30 call and the PFS-only read-through to BioNTech/BMS
summary: Summit's ivonescimab BLA (EGFR-mutant post-TKI NSCLC) received a CRL. Per Summit's release, the FDA said substantial evidence of effectiveness was not established without a statistically significant OS improvement, and PFS alone did not support a positive benefit-risk profile. Trade press citing the letter adds that 93% of PFS/death events came from China-enrolled patients and that post-hoc OS analyses were limited by differing regional data cutoffs. The FDA recommended a new multiregional trial with a significant OS result. The PFS-only read-across is real: ROSETTA Lung-02's registered Phase 3 primary is PFS by BICR, and Summit launched HARMONi-10, a PFS-primary Phase 3, after the CRL. The FDA letter PDF was not opened, and several figures conflict across trade press. The Nov 30 Summit call has not yet occurred.

angle: BIS SEA remote-access rule: data-centre and server winners and losers
summary: BIS interim final rule 'Addressing Remote Access to Advanced Semiconductors' (91 FR 74970, doc 2026-23529) was published and took effect 19 Nov 2026. It adds a worldwide end-use control (15 CFR 744.24) on chips for data centres giving more than 12M aggregate TPP to companies headquartered in Macau or Country Group D:5, requires destination licences for Indonesia, Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Brazil with a US-headquarters carve-out, and rescinds the AI Diffusion Rule. Existing providers must licence within 90 days (17 Feb 2027, my calculation). Financing and lending channels moved first: reported loan slowdowns, a stalled Bridge loan, and a paused ByteDance-linked chip loan. Asian data-centre names sold off on 17 Nov and 26 Nov, and an FT report (single source, unconfirmed) says Nvidia halted server shipments to Malaysia, Singapore, Thailand and Indonesia. Several large AI data-centre moves (GDS, DELL, SMCI, DayOne IPO) started in October, before the rule. Nothing here is a trade recommendation. Many items are second-hand or conflicting.

angle: Heron HRTX: PREM14A, record date and Nasdaq 22 Dec cliff
summary: Heron (HRTX) has not filed a PREM14A, and EDGAR shows no record date or reverse-split charter amendment. The deal documents contain no reverse split; the only charter-related item is Amendment No. 2 to the Tax Benefit Preservation Plan. The APA with CorMedix (CRMD) requires approval by a majority of outstanding common stock, not votes cast. Using the company's 190,273,587 shares, the hurdle is at least 95,136,794 FOR votes, which the June 2026 non-routine votes never reached. Voting agreements cover about 22% of shares (estimate). The Nasdaq bid-price compliance deadline of Dec 22, 2026 will pass before any meeting could occur. Heron's Hercules payoff is estimated at about $101-102m, which leaves a thin net stub after payoff. Figures marked est. are the author's own calculations.

angle: Avio/ICEYE tender: golden power, Consob and Leonardo's 10 Dec decision
summary: ICEYE, via its Italian vehicle Iris 2 S.p.A., announced a 102 notice on 17 Nov 2026 for all Avio shares at EUR 41 cash, a 21.3% premium to the EUR 33.79 official price on 16 Nov. The offer requires ICEYE to reach 66.67% and is conditional on golden power clearance without prescriptions that significantly alter its substance. As of 28 Nov, the research found no evidence that the Consob offer document was filed or approved, or that golden power notification was formally lodged. The 10 Dec Leonardo board date rests on one second-hand press report and may be only an information session. The stock traded around EUR 38.65 to 38.89, a gross spread of about 5-6% to EUR 41. Standalone downside to EUR 33.79 is about 13%. The implied failure probability is roughly 71%, but this is sensitive to assumptions.

summary: Car-Mart (CRMT) and five subsidiaries filed Chapter 11 on 24 Nov 2026 in S.D. Tex. with a stalking-horse sale to Cardinal Asset Holdings. angle: Norse 787 estate: AerCap and BOC re-leasing economics
David Jones sale: shortlist, Myer AGM and mall landlords
summary: David Jones entered voluntary administration on 5 Nov 2026, with McGrathNicol as administrator and FTI Consulting as receiver for lender Hilco (owed about $155m). Around 30 expressions of interest were reported, with indicative bids due around 30 Nov. Blundy, Kestelman, Lew, Anchorage and Myer are reported as early interest, but only Myer's status is contested and none has publicly confirmed. Nineteen stores are set to close by year-end with no signed replacement tenant found. Scentre is most exposed by store count, Vicinity by share of earnings. UBS's per-sqm figures imply a rent uplift on replacement, so any FFO pressure would have to come from downtime, capex, leasing spreads and guarantee expiry, and no FFO sensitivity was found.

angle: Peninsula Energy (PEN.AX) Lance cyber shutdown: restart and funding

angle: Sub-$1 Nasdaq convertible death spirals: VIVK, VVOS and the next victims
summary: The brief's two premises fail: VVOS was suspended on 27 Nov, before the 2 Dec meeting, and the Nasdaq Panel has not heard its case. The 2 Dec vote is a shareholder vote on a 1-for-20 to 1-for-40 reverse split, not a Panel decision. VIVK's 1-for-15 reverse split, expected 1 Dec, would lift its quoted price far above the $0.10 trigger on paper. VIVK's recent conversions appear to price below the stated $0.37 floor, which is unresolved. Several other sub-$0.30 names are already suspended or in compliance periods, and TAOP and FRSX are the next candidates to reach $0.10.
